text:
emily (support): Hey team — customer reports streaming SSE sessions drop after ~90s idle, and on reconnect the client sometimes gets a 401 which causes duplicate billing. They say last chunk sometimes truncated (partial event). Saw this behind Cloudflare -> ALB -> nginx origin. Can we triage? :wave:
li (eng-sre): thanks — any request id or example logs? is the 401 coming from our app or upstream auth?
jana (support): I have a request id: req_0a9f22. App logs show event stream resumed then AUTH_FAILED at reconnect. Server recv shows no Authorization header on the reconnect attempt.
martin (infra): interesting — that points at proxy dropping/stripping headers when connection is reused/half-closed. Cloudfront/Cloudflare and ALB have different keepalive behavior and http/2 connection coalescing can cause edge to reuse TCP for a new request without re-sending intermediate headers in some setups.
li (eng-sre): can you reproduce locally with a simple curl loop? also need pcap or tcpdump from origin side to confirm header presence on wire.
emily (support): repro steps customer provided (simplified):
```
# open SSE
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -N https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream
# wait 120s (idle)
# client reconnects to same url
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -N https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream
```
They say second curl sometimes returns 401 and server logs show no Authorization header.
li (eng-sre): can you capture the server recv (nginx access + raw headers) and Cloudflare edge logs? Specifically need the connection reuse trace (did client use connection: keep-alive or h2 multiplex?).
jana (support): attached cloudflare trace: CF reused upstream connection, then client reconnect landed on same edge, edge sent request upstream but upstream app reported no Authorization. No WAF events.
martin (infra): workaround options: 1) disable upstream connection reuse (force new conn per request) on edge/proxy (costly), 2) make client send a small heartbeat/keepalive so connection never goes idle, 3) set nginx/proxy to not buffer or to pass request headers on half-closed correctly, 4) ensure ALB health/idle timeout > client idle.
li (eng-sre): for quick repro I prepared a small test server showing header disappearance when proxy buffers and then half-closes:
```
# node express SSE test
app.get('/stream', (req,res) => {
  console.log('headers on connect', req.headers['authorization'])
  res.setHeader('Content-Type','text/event-stream')
  res.write('data: hello\\n\\n')
  // keep idle
})
```
Run behind nginx with default proxy_request_buffering on -> sometimes on reconnect req.headers['authorization'] undefined.
emily (support): customer asked if we can patch quickly, they're hitting billing by reconnect storm.
martin (infra): rolling a low-risk config change to origin nginx: set `proxy_request_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1;` and `proxy_set_header Connection "";` to avoid some buffering heuristics. That should make upstream see full headers on each request. Will also increase ALB idle timeout to 300s as an interim.
deploy-bot: deploy started: change/nginx/origin-config @deploy-6789 -> canary on origin pool (2/10 hosts) :rocket:
li (eng-sre): also adding a short-term mitigation in platform: if SSE reconnects without auth header but with session cookie we attempt to rehydrate session server-side to avoid 401 billing churn. Not ideal long term.
jana (support): noted. I'll notify customer ASAP and ask for packet captures if it persists.
emily (support): thanks. Follow-ups: 1) verify canary behavior and logs for req_0a9f22 after canary, 2) ask customer to enable client heartbeat (eg send comment event every 45s) if they can change client.
martin (infra): canary rolled: 2/2 hosts showing proxy_request_buffering off, early logs look good — reconnects now include Authorization header in server recv for the same repro.
li (eng-sre): leaving open to monitor for 24h for billing spikes. Will open a postmortem if we see recurrence.
emily (support): closing loop with customer now. Thanks all :heart:
